To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CMS has developed and successfully operated tools and procedures for the commissioning and scale validation of the distributed computing system.

the CMS distributed computing infrastructure has been successfully commissioned, that CMS computing operations are now in a state of sustainable operations and that the experiment has demonstrated that the CMS computing system can handle the computing load of data processing and user analysis at the scale of the LHC.
the CMS distributed computing infrastructure is now in place and ready for the LHC physics data taking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of the computing infrastructure and the tools used for distributed data and workload management.
improving the reliability and efficiency of the computing infrastructure and the distributed production system and with improving the user experience in accessing and analyzing data.

the commissioning of a distributed computing system with the aim of providing the CMS physics program with the computing resources it needs for the successful operation and analysis of the data produced at CERN and at the LHC experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CMS computing infrastructure has reached an unprecedented level of maturity, stability and reliability, and is now ready to support the physics analysis and data taking in 2010 and beyond.
the CMS distributed computing is now in scalable operations.
the CMS distributed computing operations are now in the final stages of commissioning and are ready for the start of data taking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CMS computing system is now in the process of commissioning, integration and scale testing, and is expected to enter a new phase of operations in early 2009, when the CMS data-taking will start.

CMS has been successful in commissioning the distributed computing system for the LHC startup in 2009, has been operating a reliable and scalable production system, and has been able to provide data access to the user analysis community.
the CMS computing system has reached the point of being able to process and analyze data at the LHC design luminosity of 1034 cm-2 s-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PADA Task Force has successfully demonstrated that a well-orchestrated and sustained effort on computing commissioning and testing is essential to ensure efficient and reliable operations of the CMS computing system.
CMS is ready for the LHC data taking with the computing infrastructure in place to process and store data, to distribute and access data, as well as to perform user analysis.
CMS computing operations can be efficiently and reliably scaled up to the LHC collision data rate.
